title: Hiring decision tension matrix + onboard contingency plan (draft)
body:
Purpose
This doc is a practical, operational playbook for hiring decisions that balances candidate quality, time-to-hire, and organizational risk. It couples a simple tension matrix (quality vs speed vs risk) with concrete onboarding contingency plans for each hiring outcome bucket. Use during final debriefs and offer planning.

Notes to self
- Intended to reduce long debates where we delay offers hoping for a marginal improvement in score.
- Keep scoring lightweight (1-5) and require explicit tie-break rationale.
- This is intentionally prescriptive: if score delta < 0.5 and time-to-fill cost > X, recommend offer. We need to finalize X (TBD).

1) The Hiring Decision Tension Matrix (how to use)
- Scoring axes (score each 1-5):
  - Candidate Fit (role competencies + cultural signals) — 1 (weak) .. 5 (exemplary)
  - Speed Imperative (how urgently team needs headcount) — 1 (not urgent) .. 5 (critical)
  - Risk Exposure (regulatory/data-sensitivity/strategic impact) — 1 (low) .. 5 (high)
- Composite decision heuristic (quick):
  - Weighted score = Candidate Fit * 0.55 + Speed Imperative * 0.25 - Risk Exposure * 0.20
  - If Weighted score >= 3.6 -> recommend extend offer
  - If Weighted score 3.0–3.6 -> convene hiring council (hiring mgr + two peers + people ops) for tie-break
  - If Weighted score < 3.0 -> archive for future, unless hiring mgr requests escalation with concrete mitigation plan

2) Interview rubric quick anchors (for consistent scoring)
- Candidate Fit (1–5) anchors:
  - 5: deep relevant experience, clear ownership stories, solved problems we currently face, shipped in scale similar to our environment
  - 4: strong match, minor gaps in domain exposure, good signals on learning velocity
  - 3: reasonable skills, needs some ramp, able to own smaller scoped projects quickly
  - 2: several skill gaps or unclear examples; risk of long ramp
  - 1: not hire
- Behavioral anchors: domain knowledge, communication, collaboration, bias toward shipping. Call out examples in debrief notes.
- Technical exercise guidance: grade on correctness (50%), systems thinking (30%), communication & tradeoffs (20%).

3) Tie-break rules (practical)
- First tie-break: team ramp cost (measured as 2-week allocation from senior engineer budget). If the team cannot absorb ramp, and candidate fit is not 4+, consider backup candidates.
- Second tie-break: runway to hire externally (how many days to re-open pipeline and probable impact). If > 30 days, favor offering to avoid lost product velocity.
- Third tie-break: diversity & long-term bench impact. If candidate increases representation in a meaningful way, document rationale and recommend offer even if weighted score marginally lower.

4) Onboard contingency plan (maps to 4 outcome buckets)
- Bucket A — Hire and high confidence (Fit >=4.2, Risk Exposure <=2): Standard offer + 30/60/90 plan.
  - Day 0 checklist: IT account provisioning, Slack add, GH access, payroll form, security AUP signed, manager intro calendar.
  - Week 1: role context 90m, shadowing schedule, immediate 2-week deliverable defined (owner + acceptance criteria).
  - Mentorship: pair with senior buddy (not direct manager), 2x/wk sync for first 4 weeks.
  - Success metric at 30 days: meaningful incremental delivery (PR merged, doc created, measurable outcome).

- Bucket B — Hire with risk mitigations (Fit 3.4–4.1 or Risk 3): Offer with conditional ramp supports
  - Additional pre-boarding: 1x extended design walkthrough with team before start, targeted learning plan (curated reading + exercises).
  - First 14 days: daily stand-up with manager + buddy available for code reviews with SLA (24h).
  - Manager commitment: reserve 10% of senior engineer time for first 30 days to de-risk onboarding.
  - If after 45 days progress < expected -> convert to 3-month performance plan OR reassign lower-impact projects.

- Bucket C — Take contractor-to-hire plan (Fit 3.0–3.5, Risk >=3 or time-to-hire is uncertain)
  - Engage as 12-week contractor with explicit milestone gates at weeks 4, 8, 12.
  - Onboarding smaller scope deliverables: week 2 integration test, week 6 feature ship, week 12 architecture handoff.
  - Legal/comply: ensure contractor agreement includes IP & confidentiality, and path to full-time if gates passed.
  - Note: this reduces pipeline risk but increases short-term cost; use only when time-to-fill is urgent or uncertainty is high.

- Bucket D — Defer / Re-open search (Fit <3.0 or Risk >=4 with limited mitigations)
  - Pause and document missing skill areas explicitly; rewrite job spec to reflect concrete deliverables.
  - Internal options: consider internal transfers or interim capacity (temp contractor, fractional PM).
  - If re-opened, set hard 30-day sprint to re-evaluate sourcing channels and interview process.

5) Offer cadence + negotiation playbook (practical scripts)
- Standard: call offer + followed by formal email within 2 hours. Key signals to accelerate offer: other active offer reported, hiring mgr explicit ask, speed imperative >=4.
- Negotiation anchors (to streamline): total comp band, signing bonus cap, relocation cap, remote vs onsite expectation. People ops negotiates above band only if hiring mgr documents strategic case.
- Quick script for counter-offer discussion: empathize -> state constraints -> offer alternative (start date flexibility, retention bonus or accelerated review at 6 months).

6) Checklist: pre-boarding and Day 0 (copyable)
- HR: send welcome packet + benefits enrollment link
- IT: device request + VPN + corp account provisioning
- Security: NDA + AUP + 2-factor auth enforced
- Manager: 30/60/90 plan + first week calendar pre-scheduled
- Team: announcement draft + onboarding buddy assigned
- Compliance (if role sensitive): additional background check + KBA access approval (track via JIRA ticket)

7) Quick calibration examples (for interviewers)
- Example A (score 4.6): Senior infra eng, shipped infra for 60k rps, clear ownership example, minor domain gap (no previous experience with our storage stack) -> Hire (Bucket A).
- Example B (score 3.3): Mid-level SWE, good coding, limited systems thinking, team has 30-day runway -> Contractor-to-hire or Bucket B depending on risk tolerance.
- Example C (score 2.4): Skill mismatch, poor behavioral anchors -> Defer and re-open search.

8) Open questions / unresolved items (action items)
- Finalize the numeric threshold for "time-to-fill cost" (X) used in tie-break rule (Action: finance + product to propose a formula) — Owner: Ethan Liu — Due: 2026-01-20
- Confirm legal language for contractor-to-hire agreements (Samir to follow up with legal) — Due: 2026-01-05
- Add a lightweight Hiring Council invite template to the hiring folder (Maya to draft) — Due: 2026-01-08

9) Immediate TODOs for this doc
- (Priya) Run this by 2 hiring managers this week for feedback and one real candidate case study to validate thresholds.
- (Ethan) Draft spreadsheet to track weighted score and hire decisions across open reqs (so we can measure how often tie-breakers used).
- (Maya) Add this doc to the hiring playbook index and mark as beta for Q1 2026.

10) Quick appendices (templates inline)
- Offer call script (short): intro -> congratulations -> role summary -> comp + start -> next steps -> ask for timeline for decision. Keep it under 6 minutes.
- Hiring council debrief form (copy-paste fields): candidate name, req, scores (fit/speed/risk), weighted score, recommended outcome, manager note (50–100 words), opps note (30–60 words), final decision and owner.

Record of changes
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (Priya)
- 2025-02-25: added tie-break rules + contractor plan (Ethan)
